why: Every id a path parameter can carry that is not a row. Malformed, absent, outside the column, and the spellings pydantic accepts where a regex would not — which is the shape of the parser divergence this suite has a named regression for. An empty id is not here on purpose: the proxy's matchers are `[^/]+` per parameter, so `/api/v1/logs/` never reaches the Go tier at all and comparing it would compare a request neither tier is asked (custom/docs/go-api-tier.md, "The wildcards that do not work"). A percent-encoded slash is not here either, and that one is a finding rather than a decision: `/api/v1/pats/..%2F..%2Fpats` is a 404 on the Python tier and a 422 here, because uvicorn unescapes the path before Starlette routes it while Go's ServeMux keeps the escaped segment as one path parameter. Whether such a request ever reaches this tier is the proxy's answer and not ours — Caddy normalises a path before its matchers see it, and this suite has no proxy in it to ask. custom/docs/go-api-tier.md records it.

variants.label: an id that is not a number
an underscore separator, which pydantic accepts
